fe: How much does a funeral cost in Colorado?

The 2026 median from 31 Colorado funeral home price lists is $1,650 for a direct cremation and $2,565 for an immediate burial, both below the national medians of $1,995 and $2,800. Those are funeral-home charges only; the cemetery bills a plot, vault, opening and closing, and headstone separately, typically $2,000–$5,000 or more.
Is final expense insurance cheaper in Colorado?

No. Premiums are set by your age, gender, tobacco use and health, and a 65-year-old in Denver is quoted from the same tables as a 65-year-old in Atlanta. What differs in Colorado is what you are insuring against: funeral-home charges here run 8 to 17% below national, so the same $10,000 policy stretches further.
How much coverage do I need for a Colorado funeral?

Add the cemetery to the funeral home. An immediate burial at Colorado’s $2,565 median plus $2,000–$5,000 of cemetery costs is $4,565–$7,565; a full traditional funeral with a viewing lands at $8,415–$11,415. Most Colorado families land between $10,000 and $15,000 once medical bills and small debts are added.
What if my family cannot find the policy after I die?

Colorado is one of the states whose insurance regulator runs a lost-policy search: the Colorado Division of Insurance’s “Find Lost Life Insurance” service, on its homepage, asks participating insurers to check their records for a deceased person. It is a backstop, not a plan — tell the person you name as beneficiary where the policy is and who the agent was.
Where is Senior Solutions Insurance located?

In Greenwood Village, Colorado, at 5775 DTC Blvd, Suite 250-S. The agent who calls you back works from that office and is licensed by the Colorado Division of Insurance, where you can verify the license.
medicare: Which Medicare Advantage plans are available in my part of Colorado?

It depends on your county. Colorado has 64, and each plan files the counties it serves, so Denver County’s list is not Larimer’s, El Paso’s or Mesa’s on the Western Slope. A licensed agent compares the plans filed for your county; the Medicare Plan Finder at medicare.gov does the same by ZIP code.
Where can I get free, independent Medicare help in Colorado?

From Colorado’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP), run by the Colorado Division of Insurance, at 1-888-696-7213, with Spanish-language counseling at 303-894-5953. It is federally funded, free, and staffed by counselors who do not sell insurance — a good second opinion on anything an agent tells you, including us.
Do I have to be in Colorado to work with Senior Solutions Insurance?

No, but Colorado is where we are: our office is at 5775 DTC Blvd in Greenwood Village and our agents are licensed by the Colorado Division of Insurance first. If you live in the state, the person who calls you back is local, and you can verify their license on the Division’s site.
How do I check that a Colorado Medicare agent is legitimate?

Use the Colorado Division of Insurance’s license verification, which is on its homepage, and ask for the agent’s license number before the call ends. If a plan was sold to you in a way that felt wrong, the same site takes the complaint, and Colorado’s SHIP at 1-888-696-7213 will tell you independently whether the plan fits.
aca: Do I buy a marketplace plan in Colorado through healthcare.gov?

No. Colorado runs its own exchange, Connect for Health Colorado, and that is where every subsidized individual and family plan in the state is sold. Senior Solutions Insurance is certified with Connect for Health Colorado and can enroll you there at no extra cost.
Has Colorado expanded Medicaid, and what is the income line?

Yes. In 2026 a single adult earning up to about $22,025, or a family of four up to about $45,540, qualifies for Health First Colorado rather than a marketplace plan. Above those figures the premium tax credit applies to a Connect for Health Colorado plan. There is no coverage gap in Colorado.
How does the premium tax credit work on Connect for Health Colorado?

Connect for Health Colorado calculates it from your household income and size and applies it to the monthly premium, so the price you see after the credit is what you pay. Because Colorado’s Medicaid line sits at about $22,025 for one person, the credit is what most single applicants above that income are shopping with.
What if I am turning 65 in Colorado?

Once Medicare Part A and Part B begin, the Connect for Health Colorado subsidy ends and Medicare becomes primary. The usual next step is a Medicare Advantage plan filed for your Colorado county, and Colorado’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program at the Division of Insurance offers free counseling on that choice; our agents in Greenwood Village handle both steps on one call.

From Tennessee’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP), run by the Department of Disability and Aging, at 1-877-801-0044 or TTY 1-800-848-0299. It is federally funded and free, and its counselors do not sell insurance, which makes it a good independent check on any agent’s advice.

Who do I complain to about a Medicare agent in Tennessee?

The Insurance Division of the Tennessee Department of Commerce and Insurance licenses agents and takes complaints through its website, where you can also verify a license. The premium after your tax credit, which is set by household income and size and applied monthly. A Tennessee household just above $15,960 for one person or $33,000 for four receives close to the largest credit available; we calculate it before comparing plans.

fe: How much does a funeral cost in Texas?

From 40 Texas funeral home price lists collected in 2026, the median direct cremation is $2,015 and the median immediate burial $2,890. Cremation is at the national median of $1,995; burial is above the national $2,800. Cemetery costs are separate and add $2,000–$5,000 or more.
Is burial or cremation the bigger saving in Texas?

Cremation. The gap between Texas’s $2,015 cremation and $2,890 burial medians is about 43% before the cemetery is counted, and choosing cremation also removes the plot, vault and marker. For a Texas family the choice between the two changes the coverage need by several thousand dollars.
How much final expense coverage does a Texas family need?

An immediate burial at Texas’s $2,890 median plus $2,000–$5,000 of cemetery costs is $4,890–$7,890. A full traditional funeral with a viewing and cemetery costs comes to $8,415–$11,415. With medical bills and small debts added, most Texas families land between $10,000 and $15,000.
Do Texas funeral costs differ between Houston and a small town?

The medians above blend both, and the spread inside Texas is wide: 40 price lists across 254 counties is a large sample precisely because the state is. The basic services fee, $2,245 at the median, is the steadiest charge; the cemetery plot is where a Houston, Dallas or Austin funeral pulls away from a rural one. Ask the funeral home for its General Price List — Texas homes must provide it — and compare that fee first.
Who regulates final expense insurance in Texas?

The Texas Department of Insurance licenses the agents and carriers; its homepage has an agent and company lookup and a complaint form. If a dispute goes further, Texas’s Office of Public Insurance Counsel represents consumers in insurance matters.
medicare: Why do my options differ from a relative’s elsewhere in Texas?

Because Medicare Advantage plans file by county, and Texas has 254 of them — more than any other state. A plan available in Dallas County may not be filed for Tarrant, and a plan in San Antonio may not exist in the Valley. A licensed agent compares only the plans filed for your county.
Where can Texans get free, independent Medicare help?

From HICAP — the Health Information, Counseling, and Advocacy Program — Texas’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program, run as a partnership of Texas Health and Human Services, Texas Legal Services Center and the Area Agencies on Aging. The Texas Medicare Help Line is 1-800-252-9240. It is federally funded and free, and the counselors do not sell insurance.
I live in a rural Texas county. Will I have any Medicare Advantage options?

Possibly fewer than a metro county, and in some of Texas’s 254 counties very few. That is exactly why the county-level check comes first; if the list for your county is short or empty, a licensed agent can tell you what the alternatives are, and HICAP’s counselors will confirm it independently.
How do I check a Texas Medicare agent’s license?

On the Texas Department of Insurance website, which has an agent and company lookup on its homepage, along with the complaint form. Ask for the license number before the call ends. Texas also has an Office of Public Insurance Counsel that represents consumers in insurance matters if a dispute goes further.
aca: I earn less than the poverty level in Texas. What can I do?

This is the Texas coverage gap. Below $15,960 for one person or $33,000 for a family of four in 2026, healthcare.gov offers no premium tax credit, and Texas Medicaid covers only specific groups because the state did not expand. Low-income parents, pregnant women, people with disabilities and adults 65 and over may still qualify for Texas Medicaid; a licensed agent will tell you honestly what exists for anyone else.
Where do Texans buy ACA marketplace coverage?

Through healthcare.gov, the federal marketplace; Texas does not run its own exchange. The application checks whether you are above the $15,960 subsidy line and calculates your premium tax credit. A licensed agent can enroll you at no extra cost.
How much will a Texas marketplace plan cost me above the poverty level?

The premium after the tax credit, set by household income and size and applied monthly. A Texas household just above $15,960 for one person or $27,320 for three receives close to the largest credit available. We calculate it first and compare plans on the net price.
I am turning 65 in Texas. Should I keep my marketplace plan?

Usually not. Once Medicare Part A and Part B begin, the premium tax credit ends and Medicare becomes primary. Texas’s Health Information, Counseling, and Advocacy Program (HICAP), run through Texas Health and Human Services at 1-800-252-9240, offers free Medicare counseling, and our agents compare the Medicare Advantage plans filed for your Texas county.

Because the funeral home is only half the bill. More reliable than for any other state in our data: 90 price lists, against 13 for North Carolina and 24 for Pennsylvania. aca: Do Californians use healthcare.gov?

Does Covered California run a longer open enrollment than healthcare.gov?

Covered California sets its own window rather than following healthcare.gov’s, and it has often run longer than the federal one. The dates are set each plan year, so we confirm the current Covered California window on the call rather than publishing one here. Two things in California do not wait for open enrollment: Medi-Cal, which enrolls year-round for adults up to about $22,025 for one person in 2026, and a special enrollment period after a qualifying event such as losing job coverage.

I live in a rural Georgia county. Will I have options?

Possibly fewer than metro Atlanta, and in some of Georgia’s 159 counties very few. That is exactly why the county check comes first: if the list is short, a licensed agent can tell you what alternatives exist, and the Georgia SHIP counselors will confirm it independently.
Who investigates a complaint about a Medicare agent in Georgia?

The Consumer Services Division of the Georgia Office of Insurance and Safety Fire Commissioner, which describes itself as the office’s investigative arm and takes complaints about agents and insurers through its website. Medicare oversees the plans themselves; Georgia’s SHIP at 1-866-552-4464 can tell you which route fits.
aca: I earn less than the poverty level in Georgia. What are my options?

Below $15,960 for one person in 2026, Georgia Access offers no premium tax credit, and Georgia did not expand Medicaid. The one Georgia-specific option is Pathways to Coverage: adults aged 19 to 64 up to 100% of the poverty level who complete 80 hours a month of work, education or community service. If you do not qualify for Pathways or a traditional Medicaid category, you are in the coverage gap, and an agent should say so plainly.
Where do Georgia residents buy marketplace coverage?

Through Georgia Access, the state’s own exchange, not healthcare.gov. Above the $15,960 subsidy line for one person, the Georgia Access application calculates your premium tax credit; a licensed agent can help you enroll there at no extra cost.
Does Georgia Access run a longer open enrollment than healthcare.gov?

Georgia Access sets its own window rather than following healthcare.gov’s, and state exchanges sometimes run longer than the federal one. The dates are set each plan year, so we confirm the current Georgia Access window on the call rather than publishing one here. Outside the window, a Georgia adult with a qualifying event still gets a special enrollment period, and an adult under $15,960 who meets the 80-hour monthly activity requirement can apply to Georgia Pathways at any time of year.
I am turning 65 in Georgia. What happens to my Georgia Access plan?

Once Medicare Part A and Part B begin, the premium tax credit ends and Medicare becomes primary, so the Georgia Access plan should end when Medicare starts. The Georgia State Health Insurance Assistance Program, run through the Division of Aging Services at 1-866-552-4464, offers free Medicare counseling, and in Georgia the county you live in — one of 159 — decides which Medicare Advantage plans are filed for you.

fe.observation: Arizona is the cheapest of the eleven states we cover, by a wide margin. Cremation at $1,240 is 38% below the national median and second-lowest in the country, behind only Nevada at $1,190; burial at $2,045 is 27% below national and the basic services fee of $1,550 is 29% below. Arizona had the second-largest net inflow of people 65 and over of any state in the 2022 Census survey, and a retiree arriving from a higher-cost state is often insuring against a bill that is smaller than they expect — at the funeral home. The cemetery still charges what it charges.
fe.coverageNote: Arizona’s low funeral-home charges mean $10,000 covers more here than almost anywhere: cremation with a memorial gathering with room to spare, and even a simple burial with cemetery costs at the lower end of the range. fe: How much does a funeral cost in Arizona?

From 29 Arizona funeral home price lists collected in 2026, the median direct cremation is $1,240 — 38% below the national median of $1,995 and the second-lowest in the country — and the median immediate burial is $2,045, 27% below the national $2,800. Cemetery costs are separate and add $2,000–$5,000 or more.
Why is cremation so inexpensive in Arizona?

The price lists show the result, not the reason: at $1,240, only Nevada ($1,190) is lower. Arizona’s non-declinable basic services fee, $1,550 against a national $2,195, is a big part of it, since that fee is inside every cremation and burial price.
How much final expense coverage does an Arizona family need?

An immediate burial at Arizona’s $2,045 median plus $2,000–$5,000 of cemetery costs is $4,045–$7,045, the lowest simplest-burial total of the eleven states we cover. A full traditional funeral with a viewing and cemetery costs comes to $8,415–$11,415. Most Arizona families are well served between $10,000 and $15,000, and cremation is comfortably within $10,000.
I moved to Arizona in retirement. Should I adjust my coverage?

Possibly downward at the funeral home, since Arizona’s charges are 27 to 38% below national, but not before checking the cemetery and any medical bills or debts the policy should also cover. A licensed agent can rework the number with you.
Are final expense rates lower in Arizona?

No. Rates are set by age, gender, tobacco use and health, not by state. What is lower in Arizona is the bill you are insuring against — a $1,240 cremation median against $1,995 nationally — which means a given policy amount goes further here than in Georgia or Pennsylvania.
medicare: With only 15 counties, are Arizona Medicare Advantage options the same everywhere?

No. Fifteen counties is fewer lists than many states, but they are still separate lists. Maricopa, Pima and Yavapai counties each have plans filed specifically for them, and the rural counties can have far fewer. A licensed agent compares the plans filed for your county.
Where can Arizonans get free Medicare counseling?

From the Arizona State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP), delivered through the Area Agencies on Aging, at azship.org or 1-800-432-4040. It is federally funded and free, and its counselors do not sell insurance.
I just moved to Arizona. Can I change my Medicare Advantage plan?

Yes. Moving to a new county is a qualifying event that opens a Special Enrollment Period, because the plans available to you have changed. Many Arizona retirees are in exactly this position; tell the agent your move date, since the window is limited, and Arizona SHIP will confirm your rights independently.
Who regulates Medicare agents in Arizona?

The Arizona Department of Insurance and Financial Institutions, which licenses insurance producers alongside the state’s financial institutions and takes complaints about both through its website. Medicare oversees the plans; Arizona SHIP at 1-800-432-4040 is the free, independent route for a question about whether a plan fits.
aca: Where do Arizona residents buy ACA coverage?

Through healthcare.gov, the federal marketplace; Arizona has no state exchange. The application checks AHCCCS eligibility first — about $22,025 for one person in 2026 — then calculates the premium tax credit for a marketplace plan. A licensed agent can enroll you at no extra cost.
Has Arizona expanded Medicaid, and what is the income line?

Yes. Household income up to about 138% of the federal poverty level — roughly $22,025 for one person or $29,863 for two in 2026 — qualifies for Medicaid through AHCCCS, so Arizona has no coverage gap. Above that, premium tax credits apply to a healthcare.gov plan.
I retired to Arizona before 65. What are my options until Medicare?

A healthcare.gov plan with the premium tax credit applied monthly, sized to your household income. Many early retirees in Arizona find that once earned income stops, their income lands just above the $22,025 AHCCCS line for one person, where the credit is close to its largest; we calculate it before comparing plans.
I am turning 65 in Arizona. What changes?

Your premium tax credit ends when Medicare Part A and Part B begin, and Medicare becomes primary. The Arizona State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP), delivered through the Area Agencies on Aging at 1-800-432-4040, offers free Medicare counseling, and if your move to Arizona is recent it may also open a Special Enrollment Period for a Medicare Advantage plan filed for your county.
